name: Li I
bio: Li I, who died in AD 827, was a T’ang poet. His poem here is the lament of a favourite who has lost the Emperor’s attention.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Cast-Off Favourite
poems.author: Li I
poems.text:
The dewdrops gleam on bright spring flowers whose scent is borne along;
Beneath the moon the palace rings with sounds of lute and song.
It seems that the clepsydra has been filled up with the sea,
To make the long long night appear an endless night to me!
